answers.answer: Rule is determined by total warriors plus buildings; the player with more than each other player rules. Ties normally mean nobody rules. Eyrie win a tie for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece in the clearing. Tokens and pawns do not count, and the Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Rule (2.5).

answers.answer: A normal move takes a positive number of your warriors or pawns along a linking path to an adjacent clearing, and you must rule the origin or destination or both. Pieces may move repeatedly, including multiple moves during one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.
answers.evidence: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; Move (4.2).

answers.answer: The defender may play one matching ambush (bird is wild); the attacker may foil it with a matching ambush. A foiled ambush deals no hits. Otherwise the defender immediately deals two hits, which are not limited by its warriors; if the attacker has no warriors or pawns left, battle ends immediately. Resolve before-roll effects, roll (higher die gives attacker hits and lower die defender hits, capped by each side's warriors), then after-roll effects. Add extra hits and subtract ignored hits; if the defender has no warriors, attacker gets one defenseless hit (Vagabond instead checks for an undamaged sword). For dealing hits, each side chooses what it removes, but must remove all its warriors before its buildings/tokens. Both sides deal counted hits even if warriors were removed after rolling. Whoever removes an enemy building or token scores one VP each, including a defender and outside battle.

Craft using crafting pieces matching the card's crafting icons at bottom left, not by paying the card's suit. Each crafting piece activates only once per turn. An item card cannot be crafted if that item is absent from the map supply. You cannot craft an identical persistent effect already in your play area.

During your Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area; remove your score marker and stop scoring VP. At the start of your own Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of that suit; bird dominance wins if you rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately. An activated card cannot be removed or replaced.

When a dominance card would enter the discard pile, place it near the map as available. During your Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so it must be paid for with a bird card; a bird card can pay for non-bird dominance.

With two players, remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and deal three cards to each player. Put one ruin in each of the four R slots. Stock the map supply with 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, and 2 coins. Faction setup order is Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, then Vagabond; this is distinct from turn order.

Only the Marquise may place pieces in the Keep's clearing, but other players may move pieces into it. If removed, the Keep cannot be placed again. When Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply; without a Keep, there is no destination for Field Hospitals. Rebuilding the Keep is therefore not permitted.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6) — Keep and Field Hospitals; Place/remove/replace (Keep placement ban).

answers.answer: Marquise Daylight starts with crafting using workshops, then up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order. Battle is one action; March is up to two moves and the compound action cannot be interrupted; Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and is allowed once per turn; Build and Overwork are also actions. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6) — Daylight and Evening.

answers.answer: Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot and choose a building type. Take the leftmost building of that type and pay the cost shown atop its column using wood in the target clearing or in other ruled clearings connected to it by an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. You need the full cost, an available building, and a legal slot. Score the VP on the track space uncovered by placing the building.

In Birdsong, first draw one card if your hand is empty (Emergency Orders). Then add one or two cards to the Decree, with at most one bird card added. Then, if you have no roosts on the map, place a roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.

Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card by columns in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order; within a column, choose the card order freely. Bird is wild. Recruit places a warrior at a roost in a clearing matching the card (two with Charismatic); Move must move at least one warrior from a matching clearing and obey normal movement restrictions; Battle must begin in a matching clearing with your warriors and an enemy; Build places a roost in a matching clearing you rule with an open slot and no existing roost. A Decree Build cannot be completed if any of those restrictions fail; inability to complete any required Decree action causes Turmoil.

In Turmoil, lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers. Discard every Decree card except the Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement, flipping all leaders face up first if none are face up. Retuck the Viziers into the new leader's columns. Daylight ends and the Eyrie proceeds to Evening, where it still scores its roost track VP, draws, and discards to five. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings.

Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. The player adds one matching hand card, with birds counting as a match, to Supporters; moving a group costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If they have no matching card including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, which draws one card from the deck into Supporters. With no base, the stack holds at most five supporters and incoming excess cards are discarded; with a base, capacity is unlimited.

In Birdsong, the Alliance may Revolt any number of times first, then Spread Sympathy any number of times. Revolt chooses a sympathetic clearing without a base matching a base still on the board, spends two matching supporters, removes all enemy pieces there, places that base, places warriors equal to matching-suit sympathy clearings (including the revolt clearing), and places one warrior in Officers; it scores normal VP for enemy buildings/tokens removed and needs a legal base slot. Spread Sympathy chooses an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to existing sympathy, or any clearing if none exists; it spends the supporter cost shown above the next sympathy token, plus one matching supporter under Martial Law when one other player has at least three warriors there. It places sympathy and scores the uncovered space. Only one sympathy may occupy a clearing; the Keep's placement ban applies.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8) — Birdsong: Revolt and Spread Sympathy.

answers.answer: Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay for Train. Evening operations are limited to the number of officers, and Organize removes an Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing to place sympathy and score the uncovered VP, with no supporter, adjacency, or Martial Law cost (but legal placement is still required). When a base is removed, discard supporters matching its clearing, including birds, remove half the officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard supporters down to five.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8) — Losing a base; Daylight; Evening.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed during this step does not add refreshes that step. Optional Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots and can enter hostile warriors, ignoring effects that prevent movement out of a clearing. A normal Daylight move exhausts one boot plus one extra boot if the destination has warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. In a forest during Evening, Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel face up and moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if possible, but does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3) — Birdsong, Daylight Move, and Evening.

answers.answer: Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing, takes one hidden item face up into Satchel or a track, and scores one VP if an item is taken; remove the ruin when its last item is taken. Quest exhausts its two listed items in a matching clearing and completes the quest; choose VP equal to the number of matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards, then draw a replacement quest. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face; ready tea, coins, or bags move to tracks if space permits.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3) — Explore, Quest, and Repair.

answers.answer: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except allied warriors removed during a battle against that same faction: if more allied warriors are removed than items damaged, it becomes Hostile at battle end; equal numbers do not trigger this. On your own turn during battle, score one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; add ordinary building/token removal points. There is no Infamy while defending on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot undo Hostility, though it can still take a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors in the clearing may you remove another piece of that faction. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3) — Strike; Relationships: Hostile and Infamy; Aid.

answers.answer: With four or more players, in its own Daylight at 10 or more VP, Vagabond may activate dominance to form a coalition with a player not already in a coalition. The partner must have the lowest VP among players other than Vagabond; Vagabond chooses among ties. Vagabond puts its score marker on the partner's faction board and stops scoring. If the partner wins, including by dominance, Vagabond also wins. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent; coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.
